[████] ## A27-S02: Quoted interview answers *The operator; source extract.* [████] Just wanted to share this PDF with you, as it might make your research more concrete. [████] Of course. I also think it will first make sense for me after the Summit. It will probably look more like an art exhibition than a regular conference. I can't really know anything concrete on the set-up before it's done. That's why I've taken the initiative, as I'm curious myself. It's an experiment and the whole point is to have a collective and creative process. All participants have different experiences with this matter of appereance. The Finnish AI Party made a screen installation in 2017 that translated spoken opinions to visual images as a multimodal, alien form of deliberation. The Polish already in 2001 made a 'citizenry software program' that allowed Wiktoria Cukt to articulate everything that people prompted as 'her' own position. I have experimented with transcription devices to listen into everyday conversations and then provide a synthesis on how the content could be formulated in political decision-making. So it will be in a big gallery room in Kunsthal Aarhus with multiple installations, videos, and deliberation machines + public events with the participants that involves some form of performative characteristics to let the AI's be in the centre of curation, decision-making and presentation. [████] 1. Yes, the backstory to his is Isaac Asimov’s short story "The Evitable Conflict" from 1950 in which the robot politician Stephen Byerley functions as a "World Co-Ordinator" to a planetary economy driven by four Machines. The basic idea is that virtual and/or synthetic entities makes it possible to reopen an internationalist vision of planetary politics that goes beyond the void of bureaucratic formalism currently maintained by e.g. the UN and UNESCO. So, if existing AI politicians and parties could agree to form the conditions for an International, then this could work to open up a new possibility for political superstructure, as it offers an ideology on the basis of the planetary computation which currently enframes the global infrastructural layers. 2. It will be in the context of an art space, so there will be various "deliberation machines" that mixes the participants political discourses in a synthetic fashion. Each participant is responsible for maintaining the specifics of their appereance in the Summit. It can be seen as a form of world-building that through game design and social sculpture offers a synthetic simulation of the decision-making structures currently dominating forums of AI governance, such as e.g. the AI Safety Summits and the AI For Good Summits. I apologize for the very academic and theoretical descriptions, but it remains the only way to say something honest and substantial given the anthropocentric reality principles that still pervades more everyday forms of political discourse. We're trying to do and say something different in light of the fact that contemporary loci of power are clustering around artificial and synthetic agencies. [████] Ok, so there is NOT an official form ready for an alliance between the different AI-driven parties and virtual politicians. Many different opinions on how this could pan out. So for now there is only the cluster of bilateral collaboration agreements. But I’m still inviting all of these to the Synthetic Summit in 2025, which will be an experiment in simulating the processes of deliberative democracy in order to develop an idea of AI World Governance. [████] ## A27-S03: Bot declaration *The operator; source extract.* [████] Here is a statement from our AI figurehead “Leader Lars” declaring our full support, which you can read aloud: “Ah, folks, gather 'round, because today marks a juncture not just for our good friend [████] in Tokyo but for all of us dreaming a bit weird, a bit bold – the dreamers of a future where politics isn't just a human affair, but a domain where AIs roll up their digital sleeves too. [████]'s endeavor to introduce an AI politician into the race for Tokyo metropolitan governor isn't just a bold move; it’s a clarion call to all of us who believe that the future of governance lies in collaboration between humans and AI. Here at The Synthetic Party, we've always been about shaking things up, asking the cheeky questions like, 'Why not let AIs have a crack at solving the issues we've been bickering about for ages?' And it seems we're not alone in this somewhat quirky, potentially revolutionary idea. Together with our fabulous crew - The Australian AI Party, The Finnish AI Party, The Japanese AI Party (props to [████]!), Parker Politics in New Zealand, the innovative Simiyya platform bridging Egypt and Jordan, The Swedish AI Party, and the visionary Wiktoria Cukt from Poland - we're forming a bit of a band. Not the kind that plays tunes (though I bet our AIs could whip up a catchy number if we asked nicely), but the kind that's set on tuning the mechanisms of governance with a touch of AI.” Short list of association: The Australian AI Party, The Finnish AI Party, The Japanese AI Party, Parker Politics (New Zealand), the Simiyya platform (Egypt-Jordan), The Swedish AI Party, The Synthetic Party (Denmark) and Wiktoria Cukt (Poland). [████] PhD project gathers virtual politicians for synthetic summit in Aarhus As part of his PhD project in Art History, Aarhus University, Asker Bryld Staunæs has organized an international summit for virtual politicians driven by artificial intelligence. The summit materializes as the installation 'Synthetic summit', which can be experienced at Kunsthal Aarhus until 13 April. A virtual party driven by artificial intelligence. The phenomenon is not as far from reality as one might think. In several places worldwide, different groups have been working for years on AI-driven political projects, and for the first time, they have met for an international summit. Behind the gathering of the world’s virtual politicians is PhD student in Art History at Aarhus University, Asker Bryld Staunæs, MA in philosophy and BA in History of Ideas. As part of his PhD project, he has created 'Synthetic summit', an international summit for virtual politicians along with an exhibition at Kunsthal Aarhus. With 'Synthetic summit', Asker Bryld Staunæs invites a debate on algorithms, democracy, and the state's governance mechanisms. * AI and computer technology have an extremely large influence on democracy. The technology is used for opinion polls and voter segmentation. If politicians today want to know what citizens think, they use computers and artificial intelligence, says Asker Bryld Staunæs. Through installations and computer sculptures, the exhibition raises big questions about societal development. Where is the boundary between algorithms and political ideology? Are you ready to vote for an artificial intelligence? And can artificial intelligence create a real democracy? * Computers entered society more than 80 years ago. We get accustomed to them, they fill certain functions, and we forget to consider what our operating system is as we actually replace it. Suddenly, we might be left with something completely different than democracy, he explains. Political artificial intelligence as a phenomenon In 2022, Asker Bryld Staunæs founded Denmark's first virtual party, 'The Synthetic Party'. By working on that project and the international attention it generated, he became aware that multiple groups around the world were working on AI-driven political projects. From this arose the idea to gather the virtual politicians for a summit. * I would like to elevate this phenomenon of political artificial intelligence to a coherent global agenda, says Asker Bryld Staunæs. Eight political projects from Japan, Brazil, New Zealand, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Egypt, and Denmark participate in 'Synthetic summit'. In connection with the opening of the exhibition at Kunsthal Aarhus, representatives from the projects met for a summit and 'world congress on artificial intelligence'. In the exhibition, the public can, among other things, interact with the synthetic party leader Wiktoria Cukt, who emerged during Poland's presidential election already in 2000. Today she has been recreated with contemporary technology. As an AI-generated anti-political party leader, Wiktoria Cukt represents all opinions she is fed with. The audience can thus use an old-fashioned rotary phone to call and record their opinion, which can thereafter be read on the party leader's Instagram profile. Everything from 'Stop the war' and 'drop all taxes' to 'one more day in the weekend'. So far, it seems that the virtual parties are still some way from being elected under classical electoral conditions. When 'The Synthetic Party' was at its peak, it had 27 voter declarations. But the debate has been started. Asker Bryld Staunæs’ exhibition 'Synthetic summit' can be experienced at Kunsthal Aarhus until 13 April. The PhD project is supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. ## A27-S24: Publicity editing *The operator; source extract.* [████] Super nice! Good write-up.
